claims.content: The cognitive error of Enneagram Type Five individuals is thinking they can understand the world as a disconnected outside observer.

claims.title: Type Five hidden complaint
claims.content: The hidden complaint of Enneagram Type Five individuals is: I am so smart that no one else can understand the things I understand or appreciate the things I know.

claims.title: Type Five healthy self-view
claims.content: The healthy sense of self for Enneagram Type Five individuals is: I am an intelligent, perceptive person.

claims.title: Type Five private mental world
claims.content: When childhood damage has compromised their confidence, Enneagram Type Five individuals may create a private mental world and master it.

claims.title: Type Five childhood rejection
claims.content: Enneagram Type Five individuals feel ambivalently identified with both parents or parent figures, and at a deep level feel rejected by both.

claims.title: Type Five self-awareness saving grace
claims.content: Awareness of their own thought processes may help average Enneagram Type Five individuals avoid further deterioration and return to a more balanced state.

claims.title: Type Five basic fear
claims.content: The basic fear of Enneagram Type Five individuals is of being helpless, useless, and incapable.

claims.title: Type Five niche search
claims.content: Enneagram Type Five individuals look for an unclaimed niche that gives them a sense of place and belonging, and they do not believe they can engage deeply in sustainable relationships until they master that niche.

claims.title: Type Five anger under control
claims.content: Disagreements or fears of control by others can cause Enneagram Type Five individuals to lose their tempers, revealing underlying anger, rejection, and powerlessness.

claims.title: Type Five conceptualizing distortion
claims.content: Excessive conceptualizing can lead Enneagram Type Five individuals to distorted perception and a growing loss of confidence.

claims.title: Type Five acting out like Eight
claims.content: Average Enneagram Type Five individuals may act out average Type Eight behaviors, usually with trusted friends and intimates, becoming assertive and defiant.

claims.title: Type Five security through wisdom
claims.content: Enneagram Type Five individuals feel more capable and secure when they use their wisdom compassionately for the good of the world.

claims.title: Type Five social withdrawal
claims.content: Enneagram Type Five individuals may go into so much depth on their interests that they become socially and physically absent, and may be awkward or unaware of social conventions.

claims.title: Type Five overthinking
claims.content: Average to unhealthy Enneagram Type Five individuals think too much, applying concepts in inappropriate categories and circumstances, and become lost in their own thought processes.

claims.title: Type Five structural pattern
claims.content: The keynote of Enneagram Type Five is concentration, with the mind focused on comprehending reality but driven by subjective impulses, including aggression.

claims.title: Type Five paradoxical pattern
claims.content: Enneagram Type Five individuals may show paradoxical curiosity and withdrawal, involvement and detachment, and aggression and fear of aggression.

claims.title: Type Five defense mechanisms
claims.content: Enneagram Type Five individuals mainly use displacement, projection, and isolation as defense mechanisms.

claims.title: Average Type Six security seeking
claims.content: Average Enneagram Type Six individuals begin to doubt themselves and seek reassurance, alliances, and authorities for security.

claims.title: Healthy Type Six work habits
claims.content: Healthy Enneagram Type Six individuals are hardworking, dependable, cooperative, and committed to quality craftsmanship.

claims.title: Healthy Type Six traits
claims.content: Healthy Enneagram Type Six individuals are engaging, friendly, reliable, and trustworthy, and they follow through on their commitments.

claims.title: Type Five loss of reality contact
claims.content: Enneagram Type Five individuals who disengage from reality may lose touch with objective facts and become lost in their inner world.

claims.title: Type Six commitments under pressure
claims.content: As anxiety grows, average Enneagram Type Six individuals take on more commitments and feel pressured by others' expectations.

claims.title: Unhealthy Type Six dependence
claims.content: Unhealthy Enneagram Type Six individuals may seek a stronger authority or belief for rescue, and may humiliate themselves before an authority figure.

claims.title: Type Six stress reactions
claims.content: Under stress, average Enneagram Type Six individuals may become indecisive, evasive, and passive-aggressive, giving mixed signals.

claims.title: Average Type Six anxiety pattern
claims.content: Average Enneagram Type Six individuals feel anxious about the future and try to cover all the bases while still feeling insecure.

claims.title: Type Five withdrawal undermines desire
claims.content: Enneagram Type Five individuals who withdraw into mental constructs undermine their Basic Desire to be competent and capable.

claims.title: Unhealthy Type Six patterns
claims.content: Unhealthy Enneagram Type Six individuals may become panicky, insecure, depressed, and paranoid, and may see others as enemies.

claims.title: Healthy Sixes: stable and supportive
claims.content: Healthy Enneagram Type Sixes become emotionally stable, supportive, and reassuring, and their anxiety has largely resolved.

claims.title: Unhealthy Sixes: dishonesty under pressure
claims.content: Unhealthy Enneagram Type Sixes that move toward Three may become dishonest and unprincipled to preserve their position or security.

claims.title: Basic Fear defined for Enneagram
claims.content: Basic Fear is the core fear that motivates an Enneagram type; for Type Six, it is being without support and guidance.

claims.title: Healthy Sixes ground in presence
claims.content: Healthy Enneagram Type Sixes that move toward Nine find stable inner support and become grounded in their physical presence in the here and now.

claims.title: Sixes doubt and belief attachment
claims.content: Enneagram Type Six is often plagued by doubt and can become emotionally attached to a plausible belief system.

claims.title: Six basic fear: no support
claims.content: Basic Fear of Enneagram Type Six is being without support and guidance.

claims.title: Sixes seek trusted authority
claims.content: Enneagram Type Sixes seek security, safety, and an authority they can trust, because they lack a felt sense of inner guidance.

claims.title: Sixes' childhood protective figure
claims.content: Enneagram Type Sixes look to an idealized protective authority figure, often the father, for guidance and support in childhood.

claims.title: Six basic desire: support
claims.content: Basic Desire of Enneagram Type Six is to have support and guidance.

claims.title: Sixes shut down with intimates
claims.content: Average Enneagram Type Sixes can act out average Type Nine behaviors with trusted intimates, shutting down and numbing out.

claims.title: Type Six in Thinking Triad
claims.content: Enneagram Type Six is the primary type in the Thinking Triad.

claims.title: Very unhealthy Sixes: violent striking out
claims.content: Very unhealthy Enneagram Type Sixes may strike out violently at authorities or people who symbolize a great betrayal.

claims.title: Gendered patterns in Six pathology
claims.content: Male Enneagram Type Sixes are more likely to commit irrational violence, while female Sixes more often use a charming false persona and target perceived oppressors in focused, personal ways.

claims.title: Sixes seek outside direction
claims.content: Enneagram Type Six lacks clear inner guidance and looks outside itself for direction and reassurance.

claims.title: Average Sixes: anxious but persevering
claims.content: Average Enneagram Type Sixes are often visibly anxious and self-doubting, yet they persevere and meet their commitments.

claims.title: Sixes move toward Three
claims.content: When stress overwhelms their defenses, average Enneagram Type Sixes may move toward Three by hiding in work and projecting confidence.

claims.title: Type Six: using anxiety constructively
claims.content: Sixes experience anxiety as a force they can use to boost themselves to higher accomplishment and independence when they experience it consciously in the present.

claims.title: Type Six: oscillating defensive behavior
claims.content: Sixes alternate between being defensive and resisting others' influence, and acting forcefully to show they are not dependent.

claims.title: Sixes: reassurance undermines confidence
claims.content: Sixes rely on others for reassurance, which in the long run undermines their self-confidence.

claims.title: Type Seven: versatile healthy achievers
claims.content: Healthy Sevens are practical, productive, and prolific people of action and energy who become versatile across many areas of life.

claims.title: Type Six: healthy sense of self
claims.content: Sixes' healthy sense of self is the belief, "I am a committed, dependable person."

claims.title: Type Six: key defense mechanisms
claims.content: Sixes' key defense mechanisms are identification, displacement, and projection.

claims.title: Type Six: basic desire and fear
claims.content: Sixes' Basic Desire is to find support, guidance, and security, and their Basic Fear is being abandoned and without support.

claims.title: Type Six: characteristic temptation
claims.content: Sixes' characteristic temptation is to rely on others to help them become independent.

claims.title: Type Seven: healthy enthusiasm
claims.content: Healthy Sevens are highly responsive, free-spirited, and enthusiastic about their experiences.

claims.title: Type Seven collapse and self-destructive risk
claims.content: When defenses collapse, Type Sevens may fall into severe depression, despair, and self-destructive behavior, including suicide.

claims.title: Type Seven scattered energy and inner guidance
claims.content: Type Sevens, out of touch with Inner Guidance, tend to try everything and scatter their energy because they do not know what will fulfill them.

claims.title: Type Seven stress shift toward Type One
claims.content: Under stress, average Type Sevens take on some Type One behaviors, ordering their affairs in rigid and self-critical ways that they soon abandon.

claims.title: Unhealthy Type Seven addictions and excess
claims.content: Unhealthy Type Sevens may fall into addictions or reckless overspending or gambling, and can become dissipated and callous.

claims.title: Type Seven anxiety and distraction
claims.content: As anxiety escalates, Type Sevens become hyperactive, scattered, and distracted, and use constant stimulation to avoid painful feelings.

claims.title: Type Seven average restlessness and focus
claims.content: Average Type Sevens become restless, want more options, and grow less focused, often struggling to follow through on projects.

claims.title: Unhealthy Type Seven behavior toward others
claims.content: Unhealthy Type Sevens become rude, abusive, and easily frustrated, and deny responsibility for problems they create.

claims.title: Type Seven integration toward Type One
claims.content: In integration, Type Sevens who take on healthy Type One traits can recognize that they need to slow down their activities to find real fulfillment.

claims.title: Type Seven defense mechanisms
claims.content: Enneagram Type Seven's key defense mechanisms are repression, externalization, and acting out.

claims.title: Type Seven average Five behaviors
claims.content: Average Enneagram Type Sevens can act out Type Five behaviors, mostly with trusted friends and intimates.

claims.title: Type Seven characteristic temptation
claims.content: Enneagram Type Seven's characteristic temptation is to think that fulfillment is somewhere else.

claims.title: Type Seven healthy movement to Five
claims.content: Healthy Enneagram Type Sevens who move to Type Five become more deeply involved in their experiences and learn to concentrate and stay focused.

claims.title: Type Seven hidden complaint
claims.content: Enneagram Type Seven's hidden complaint is "I am happy, although I would be a lot happier if I got everything I wanted."

claims.title: Type Seven basic fear
claims.content: Enneagram Type Seven's basic fear is being trapped in pain and deprivation.

claims.title: Type Seven basic desire
claims.content: Enneagram Type Seven's basic desire is to be satisfied and content, with its needs fulfilled.

claims.title: Type Seven healthy self-view
claims.content: Enneagram Type Seven's healthy sense of self is "I am a happy, enthusiastic person."

claims.title: Type Seven childhood pattern
claims.content: Enneagram Type Seven's childhood pattern centers on a fear of being deprived by nurturers, which causes chronic frustration.

claims.title: Type Seven deterioration pattern
claims.content: Enneagram Type Seven, when deteriorating, flees from self, anxiety, and aloneness while demanding that the material world, including other people, meet all its needs.

claims.title: Saving Grace for Type Seven
claims.content: In the Enneagram, Saving Grace for average Type Sevens is their genuine enthusiasm and appreciation of life, which can keep them from sliding into escapism or manic hyperactivity.

claims.title: Type Seven structural keynote
claims.content: The keynote of Enneagram Type Seven is responsiveness, since its energy is mostly invested in external stimulation.

claims.title: Sevens' unwillingness to commit
claims.content: Average to unhealthy Sevens who become unwilling to say no to their whims and impulses cross a boundary that can have serious consequences.

claims.title: Sevens' cognitive error about the future
claims.content: Average to unhealthy Sevens believe satisfaction comes from anticipating the future rather than from the present moment, which undermines their satisfaction.

claims.title: Sevens consume experiences without internalizing
claims.content: Average to unhealthy Type Sevens consume experiences with little personal internalization and feel continually frustrated.

claims.title: Sevens' impulsive pattern worsens basic fear
claims.content: If average to unhealthy Sevens keep jumping impulsively between activities, they increasingly bring about their Basic Fear of being trapped in pain and deprivation.

claims.title: Healthy Eights stand up for themselves
claims.content: Healthy Type Eights have learned to stand up for themselves and what they need and want.

claims.title: Unhealthy Eights develop outlaw mentality
claims.content: Unhealthy Type Eights feel deeply betrayed and develop an outlaw mentality, respecting no law or limit on their behavior.

claims.title: Sevens' path to health
claims.content: The way for Sevens to become healthier is to become still enough inside to grieve their losses and recognize the inner quiet where true fulfillment can be found.

claims.title: Eights fear dependence on others
claims.content: Average Type Eights want to be as independent and autonomous as possible, fearing dependence on others.

claims.title: Eights dominate under stress
claims.content: As stress mounts, average Type Eights become more self-protective and seek to dominate their environment, including others.

claims.title: Eight underlying rejection and needs
claims.content: Type Eight individuals' Two-like behaviors reveal underlying feelings of rejection, suppressed needs for closeness and nurturing, and sadness about lost innocence.

claims.title: Eight unhealthy delusion and recklessness
claims.content: Unhealthy Type Eight individuals may develop delusions of omnipotence and invincibility, become reckless, and in danger may vengefully try to destroy what does not conform to their will.

claims.title: Eight acting out Two behaviors
claims.content: Type Eight individuals may act out average Type Two behaviors, mostly with trusted friends and intimates, by providing good things for people they care about.

claims.title: Eight aggression and repression issues
claims.content: Type Eight individuals may show issues with aggression (rage) and repression of vulnerability.

claims.title: Eight little protector role
claims.content: Young Type Eight children learn to get nurturance by becoming the strong, independent little protector who takes care of others.

claims.title: Eight toddler will-testing origin
claims.content: Type Eight children may test wills against their mothers in toddlerhood, asserting independence, which can be interpreted as rejection.

claims.title: Unhealthy Eight collapse toward Five
claims.content: Under extreme stress, unhealthy Type Eight individuals may move toward unhealthy Type Five, becoming hopeless, distrustful, and nihilistically isolated.

claims.title: Eight compulsion to act
claims.content: Type Eight individuals feel compelled to act on instinctive energy, sometimes without fully considering the consequences.

claims.title: Average Eight action and power struggles
claims.content: Average Type Eight individuals are people of action who assert themselves openly, take strong positions, and sometimes enter power struggles to seek justice or protect their self-interest.

claims.title: Unhealthy Eight domination and enemies
claims.content: Unhealthy Type Eight individuals may become secretive, remote, cynical, and pessimistic, try to dominate their environment, and often make real enemies.

claims.title: Eight boundary maintenance and testing
claims.content: Type Eight individuals use instinctual energy to maintain their boundaries and to test the boundaries of others.

claims.title: Eight childhood ambivalence toward nurturer
claims.content: Type Eight individuals often grow up ambivalent toward their nurturer, usually the mother or a mother figure, and with largely unconscious feelings of rejection.

claims.title: Eight instinctive center and security point
claims.content: Type Eight is a Enneagram type whose instinctive center gives vitality, with Security Point noted as a separate section in the file.

claims.title: Healthy Eight integration toward Two
claims.content: Healthy Type Eight individuals who move toward Type Two discover suppressed feelings of compassion and use their strength to support and uplift others.

claims.title: Eight early responsibility and suppressed needs
claims.content: Many Type Eight individuals develop adult responsibility or burden at an early age and suppress their fear, vulnerability, and emotional need.

claims.title: Eight disintegration toward Five
claims.content: When overwhelmed, average Type Eight individuals may adopt behaviors of average Type Five, becoming more reclusive, emotionally withdrawn, and strategic.

claims.title: Eight strong reactions read as rejection
claims.content: Type Eight children with stronger wills and instinctual drives often produce stronger emotional reactions in caretakers, which they may interpret as rejection.

claims.title: Eight sentimentality toward children and pets
claims.content: In secure settings, Type Eight individuals may show unembarrassed sentimentality, especially toward children or pets, and want to care for them.

claims.title: Integrated Eight expression and nurturing
claims.content: Integrating Type Eight individuals express feelings more freely, nurture others, and accept nurturing without feeling weakened.

claims.title: Eight identity through assertion
claims.content: Type Eight individuals maintain their identity by forcefully asserting themselves while seeking not to be affected or controlled by their environment.

claims.title: PT citation reference pages
claims.content: PT is a reference cited in the Type Eight childhood pattern passage, at pages 304 to 306.

claims.title: Eight pursuit of intensity
claims.content: Type Eight individuals constantly seek intensity, and their sense of identity is sustained by intensifying their reactions to whatever they do.

claims.title: Eight instinctive impulse acting out
claims.content: Type Eight individuals tend to act out instinctive impulses rather than contain or feel them, which gives them strong vitality.

claims.title: Eight defense mechanisms
claims.content: Enneagram Type Eight's key defense mechanisms are repression, displacement, and denial.

claims.title: Basic Fear defined
claims.content: Basic Fear is the core fear a type holds in this typology; for Enneagram Type Eight it is the fear of being harmed or controlled, or of violation.

claims.title: Eight autonomy and dependence paradox
claims.content: Average to unhealthy Enneagram Type Eights want to be utterly autonomous, yet want to become so powerful that others depend on them.

claims.title: Eight cognitive error defined
claims.content: Enneagram Type Eights' cognitive error is identifying themselves with their ability to assert themselves independently of others.

claims.title: Eight characteristic temptation
claims.content: Enneagram Type Eight's characteristic temptation is to think they are completely independent and self-sufficient.

claims.title: Eight secondary motivations
claims.content: Enneagram Type Eight's secondary motivations include asserting themselves, proving their abilities, being respected, and dominating their environment.

claims.title: Eight outward aggression pattern
claims.content: Enneagram Type Eights' primary force is aggression directed outward at the external world by a strong ego.

claims.title: Eight confrontation increases threat
claims.content: Enneagram Type Eights' confrontational attitude increases the likelihood that others will harm or control them.

claims.title: Eight need equated with weakness
claims.content: Enneagram Type Eights equate need with weakness, which leads to emotional isolation, resentment of others, and efforts to control everything.

claims.title: Eight hidden complaint
claims.content: Enneagram Type Eight's hidden complaint is "I am fighting for my own survival, and others would take advantage of me if I let them."

claims.title: Nine healthy traits: receptive and serene
claims.content: Healthy Enneagram Type Nines are receptive, open, emotionally stable, and serene.

claims.title: Eight healthy sense of self
claims.content: Enneagram Type Eight's healthy sense of self is the statement "I am a strong, assertive person."

claims.title: Eight rejection of vulnerability
claims.content: Less healthy Enneagram Type Eights reject their own fear, vulnerability, and neediness, which makes them insensitive to these qualities in others.

claims.title: Unhealthy Eight dependence and fear
claims.content: Less healthy Enneagram Type Eights become dependent on others for protection and live in constant fear of retribution.

claims.title: Nine healthy influence on groups
claims.content: Healthy Enneagram Type Nines are optimistic, reassuring, and supportive, and they harmonize groups and bring people together.

claims.title: Eight basic desire: self-protection
claims.content: Enneagram Type Eight's basic desire is to protect themselves and their independence.

claims.title: Type Nine easygoing outlook
claims.content: Average Enneagram Type Nine people are easygoing and agreeable, keep a positive outlook, and try to stay unruffled by life's ups and downs.

claims.title: Type Nine strengths in mediation
claims.content: Enneagram Type Nine people are steady, reassuring, and good mediators, negotiators, and counselors.

claims.title: Type Nine unexpressed rage
claims.content: Unhealthy Enneagram Type Nine people hold enormous unexpressed rage and can become highly depressed.

claims.title: Type Nine in Instinctive Triad
claims.content: Enneagram Type Nine is the primary type of the Instinctive Triad and is the type most out of touch with its own instinctual drives.

claims.title: Type Nine deflection through beliefs
claims.content: Average Enneagram Type Nine people use beliefs, stock sayings, and airtight philosophies to deflect others and defend against change.

claims.title: Type Nine at best
claims.content: At their best, Enneagram Type Nine people become self-possessed, content, and powerfully alive.

claims.title: Type Nine numbness as relaxation
claims.content: Enneagram Type Nine people may confuse numbness with relaxation and seek numbness through television, potboiler novels, and substance abuse.

claims.title: Type Nine repressed assertiveness
claims.content: Enneagram Type Nine people repress assertive impulses and their sense of self and independence.

claims.title: Type Nine identification with others
claims.content: Enneagram Type Nine people tend to live vicariously through a perceived stronger or more passionate person to replace the stimulation their instinctive energy would provide.

claims.title: Type Nine conflict avoidance
claims.content: Average Enneagram Type Nine people become self-effacing and agreeable on the surface to avoid conflict, while keeping an inner resistance.

claims.title: Type Nine dissociation
claims.content: Unhealthy Enneagram Type Nine people may dissociate to a degree that leaves them unable to function.

claims.title: Type Nine vicarious living
claims.content: Average Enneagram Type Nine people may accept conventional roles and expectations without question and live vicariously through others.

claims.title: Type Nine avoidance of problems
claims.content: Average Enneagram Type Nine people suppress their desires and walk away from conflicts instead of addressing problems.

claims.title: Type Nine reactive stress pattern
claims.content: Under stress, Type Nines may become reactive and defiant like Sixes when their problems are interpersonal, which gives short-term relief but does not resolve the underlying conflicts.

claims.title: Type Nine stress response
claims.content: Under stress, unhealthy Nines can become extremely stubborn and resistant to experiencing their inner pain and anxiety, and they use denial and dissociation until they can no longer function.

claims.title: Type Nine security point
claims.content: Under security, Type Nines can act out average Three behaviors, most often with trusted friends and intimates, such as adapting to others' expectations and focusing on image.

claims.title: Type Nine defense mechanisms
claims.content: Type Nine's key defense mechanisms are repression, dissociation, and denial.

claims.title: Type Nine childhood connection
claims.content: Type Nines are connected with both parents or parent figures, and as young children they take on the emotional tone of their family and the expectations of both parents.

claims.title: Type Nine growth direction
claims.content: Healthy Type Nines who move toward Three become interested in developing themselves, take control of their lives, and invest time in activities that hone their talents.

claims.title: Type Nine basic fear
claims.content: Enneagram Type Nine has the basic fear of loss and separation, and of fragmentation.

claims.title: Type Nine healthy self-view
claims.content: Type Nine's healthy sense of self is the statement "I am a peaceful, easygoing person."

claims.title: Type Nine inner peace approach
claims.content: Type Nines try to bring ease and simplicity to external affairs by cultivating inner peace.

claims.title: Type Nine hidden complaint
claims.content: Type Nine's hidden complaint is "I am content with the way things are, although everyone else is always pressuring me to change."

claims.title: Type Nine growth outcomes
claims.content: As their sense of self develops, Type Nines become more assertive, independent, and self-assured, and their self-esteem increases.

claims.title: Type Nine basic desire
claims.content: Enneagram Type Nine has the basic desire for peace of mind and wholeness.

claims.title: Type Nine avoidance of assertion
claims.content: For average Type Nines, directness or taking a strong position feels like an aggressive act, and they believe asserting themselves risks disrupting the harmony in their relationships.

claims.title: Type Nine core search
claims.content: Type Nines seek harmony and stability, desire oneness and wholeness for themselves and others, and perceive an ideal order.

claims.title: Type Nine childhood retreat
claims.content: As children, Type Nines who feel crowded by family demands retreat to imagination, nature, or other children, or withdraw emotionally, and try to be invisible to avoid adding conflict.

claims.title: Nine inner life dominated by fantasy
claims.content: Enneagram Type Nine people's inner life is dominated by fantasy, and they remain defended against reality.

claims.title: Nine defenses cause isolation
claims.content: The defenses Enneagram Type Nine people use to protect their inner comfort distance them from others and can lead to isolation.

claims.title: Ones value truth and justice
claims.content: Healthy Enneagram Type One people treat truth and justice as primary values.

claims.title: Nine passivity causes conflict
claims.content: Enneagram Type Nine people's passivity, unwillingness to deal with reality, and unconscious anger inevitably cause conflicts with others.

claims.title: Average Ones feel responsible to improve
claims.content: Average Enneagram Type One people become dissatisfied with reality and feel personally responsible for improving everything.

claims.title: Ones at their best
claims.content: Enneagram Type One people at their best become extraordinarily wise, humane, and transcendentally realistic.

claims.title: Nines say yes when meaning no
claims.content: Enneagram Type Nine people often say yes when they mean no, which avoids short-term conflict but leaves them angry.

claims.title: Nine keynote is self-effacement
claims.content: The keynote of Enneagram Type Nine is self-effacement.

claims.title: Repressed anger leads to resistance
claims.content: For Enneagram Type Nine people, repressed anger is the first step toward resistance, depression, and dissociation.

claims.title: Ones hold strong convictions
claims.content: Enneagram Type One people are conscientious, hold strong personal convictions, and have an intense sense of right and wrong.

claims.title: Type One: standards and correcting
claims.content: Enneagram Type One people strive to maintain high standards and feel a need to explain, remedy, and correct errors.

claims.title: Type One: fear of mistakes
claims.content: Enneagram Type One people become more afraid of making mistakes as they express their views and standards more.

claims.title: Type One: repressed instincts
claims.content: Enneagram Type One people often repress their instinctive impulses and rely on strong positions and convictions to compensate.

claims.title: Type One stress direction: Four
claims.content: Under stress, Enneagram Type One people move toward unhealthy Type Four behaviors, including self-pity and withdrawal.

claims.title: Unhealthy Type One: severe depression risk
claims.content: Unhealthy Enneagram Type One people may experience severe depression, self-reproach, and suicidal thoughts when they deteriorate to unhealthy Type Four.

claims.title: Type One integration direction: Seven
claims.content: Healthy Enneagram Type One people who move toward Type Seven accept imperfection, relax, and become more joyous and spontaneous.

claims.title: Unhealthy Type One: rigid judgment
claims.content: Unhealthy Enneagram Type One people are extremely dogmatic, closed-minded, self-righteous, and intolerant.

claims.title: Average Type One over-responsibility
claims.content: Average Enneagram Type One people come to believe that everything falls on them personally to improve, so they become fixated on correcting and criticizing.

claims.title: Type One keynote objectivity
claims.content: Enneagram Type One's keynote is objectivity, with an aim to be rational, fair-minded, and unmoved by personal desire.

claims.title: Superego as Inner Critic
claims.content: In the Enneagram Type One description, the superego is also called the Inner Critic, the internal judge of what is good and in balance.

claims.title: Type One basic desire
claims.content: Enneagram Type One's basic desire is to be good and to have integrity.

claims.title: Type One basic fear
claims.content: Enneagram Type One's basic fear is of being bad, imbalanced, defective, or corrupt.

claims.title: Type One moral obligation temptation
claims.content: Enneagram Type One's characteristic temptation is an extreme sense of personal moral obligation.

claims.title: Type One hidden complaint
claims.content: Enneagram Type One's hidden complaint is "I am right most of the time, and it would be a better world if people listened to what I tell them."

claims.title: Type One saving grace
claims.content: Enneagram Type One's saving grace is a healthy capacity for reason and moderation that can help them return to a healthier state.

claims.title: Type One core traits
claims.content: Enneagram Type One has a set of core traits: basic fear, basic desire, healthy sense of self, hidden complaint, characteristic temptation, and key defense mechanisms.

claims.title: Type One defense mechanisms
claims.content: Enneagram Type One's key defense mechanisms are repression, reaction formation, and displacement.

claims.title: Type One childhood guidance experience
claims.content: Young Enneagram Type One children often felt that guidance, structure, and support in early childhood were too strict, too arbitrary, too vague, or lacking.

claims.title: Type One healthy self-view
claims.content: Enneagram Type One's healthy sense of self is "I am a reasonable, objective person."

claims.title: Integrating Type One awareness
claims.content: Integrating Enneagram Type One people increasingly recognize the perfection that is already present in their lives.

claims.title: Type One concern for consequences
claims.content: Enneagram Type One people are most concerned about the consequences of their actions among all personality types, because they are rational and logical.

claims.title: Superego dependence blocks integrity
claims.content: Enneagram Type One Ones who depend on the superego's evaluation of themselves and reality will not find the integrity and wisdom they seek.

claims.title: Levels of Development defined
claims.content: The Levels of Development are the nine stages within each Enneagram type, forming a continuum from healthy to average to unhealthy states.

claims.title: Superego judgments create inner division
claims.content: Enneagram Type One's superego judgments create inner division and conflict within the self.

claims.title: Superego as sole arbiter
claims.content: If Enneagram Type One Ones continue to treat the superego as the sole arbiter of truth and right action, they will gradually become caught in their Basic Fear of being bad, defective, or corrupt.

claims.title: Early type descriptions were brief
claims.content: Early Enneagram type descriptions were short and impressionistic, and they lacked enough detail for a deep understanding of each type.

claims.title: Integrity defined as wholeness
claims.content: Integrity is a function of wholeness, meaning to have integrity is to be without inner division or conflict.

claims.title: Thematic descriptions lacked structure
claims.content: Don Riso found that a thematic approach to writing type descriptions involved much repetition and lacked an overall structure.

claims.title: People shift along Continuum
claims.content: People shift up and down the Continuum, sometimes spiraling downward into neurosis or moving upward toward health and integration.

claims.title: Levels as key to describing types
claims.content: Levels of Development are the key to describing personality types economically by revealing larger patterns beneath everyday confusion.

claims.title: Nine Levels across Continuum
claims.content: Each personality type's Continuum has nine Levels, grouped as healthy (Levels 1 to 3), average (Levels 4 to 6), and unhealthy (Levels 7 to 9).

claims.title: Each Level is a process
claims.content: Each Level is a specific psychological and interpersonal process that arises at that point along the Continuum.

claims.title: Type Three sorting produced nine piles
claims.content: Sorting the traits of type Three produced nine piles that appeared to form a gradation.

claims.title: Psychic Structures: definition
claims.content: Psychic Structures are unpublished abstract models that underlie the Levels and give the rationale for each trait's placement within each type.

claims.title: Nine trait piles in three groups
claims.content: The traits of the personality types consistently fell into nine piles, which the author divided into three groups of three: healthy, average, and unhealthy.

claims.title: Continuum: sequence of nine Levels
claims.content: The Continuum is the sequence of nine Levels that describes how each personality type moves from healthy to unhealthy.

claims.title: Index card sorting method
claims.content: The author wrote each trait or observation about the personality types on index cards and sorted them so that categories could emerge.

claims.title: Level titles as signposts
claims.content: Each Level has a two- or three-word title that serves as a descriptive signpost for what happens at that stage along the Continuum.

claims.title: Levels as parts and subtypes
claims.content: Each Level can be described both as an integral part of the entire personality type and as a discrete personality subtype unique to itself.

claims.title: Levels of Development: definition
claims.content: Levels of Development are the graded stages along each personality type's Continuum, from healthy to unhealthy.

claims.title: Levels discovered in 1977
claims.content: The author discovered the Levels of Development in 1977, after two years of organizing observations into coherent descriptions.

claims.title: Traits change across Levels
claims.content: Enneagram types change in behavior at different Levels, so a type's characteristics can become their opposite at unhealthy Levels.

claims.title: Type Two Level ranges
claims.content: Enneagram Type Two has a healthy-to-unhealthy progression of Levels: a set of nine Level names, with three Levels each in healthy, average, and unhealthy ranges.

claims.title: Type Two parallel Levels 1, 4, 7
claims.content: Levels 1, 4, and 7 of Enneagram Type Two are parallel, moving from unconditional love to people pleasing to manipulation.

claims.title: Levels move in both directions
claims.content: Movement along the Levels of Development can go in both directions, and each person oscillates up and down the Levels.

claims.title: Type Two parallel Levels 2, 5, 8
claims.content: Levels 2, 5, and 8 of Enneagram Type Two are parallel, moving from empathy to intrusiveness to coercion.

claims.title: Eight traits by health level
claims.content: Healthy Enneagram Eights are the most big-hearted and constructive of the types, while unhealthy Eights are full of rage and extremely destructive and hard-hearted.

claims.title: Eighty-one Levels of Development
claims.content: The Enneagram describes eighty-one Levels of Development, which are nine Levels for each of nine personality types.

claims.title: Type Two deterioration summary
claims.content: Enneagram Type Two moves from healthy disinterested altruism, compassionate concern, and generosity to average effusive friendliness, possessiveness, and self-importance, then to unhealthy manipulation, coercive dominance, and psychosomatic suffering.

claims.title: Types require all nine Levels
claims.content: Each Enneagram personality type is the sum of its nine Levels of Development, so a type should not be assigned from a handful of traits.

claims.title: Typing needs many traits
claims.content: Each Enneagram type is a continuum of many interrelated traits and motivations, and many of them must be considered before self-identification or diagnosis.

claims.title: Type Two Level names
claims.content: Enneagram Type Two has nine Levels: Disinterested Altruist, Caring Person, Nurturing Helper, Effusive Friend, Possessive Intimate, Self-important Saint, Self-Deceptive Manipulator, Coercive Dominator, and Psychosomatic Victim.

claims.title: Upward movement means health
claims.content: Movement up the Levels of Development is movement toward increasing psychological health and balance.

claims.title: Levels are a map only
claims.content: The Levels of Development are a map of the territory, not the territory itself, and real people are not as structured or predictable as the Levels suggest.

claims.title: Health level causes mistyping
claims.content: A healthy Enneagram Eight and an unhealthy Eight may seem so different that they are mistyped or misunderstood.

claims.title: Type Two parallel Levels 3, 6, 9
claims.content: Levels 3, 6, and 9 of Enneagram Type Two are parallel, moving from generosity to uninvited self-sacrifice to feeling victimized.

claims.title: Levels presented top down
claims.content: The Enneagram Levels of Development are presented from the top down as a progressive deterioration toward increasing unhealth, for descriptive economy.

claims.title: Level 5: control of others
claims.content: At Level 5 (Interpersonal Control), the ego inflates as a person tries to control others to obtain his or her Basic Desire.

claims.title: Basic Fear: childhood loss of contact
claims.content: Basic Fear is a fear that arises in childhood from the loss of contact with the ground of our being.

claims.title: Level 3: persona and defenses
claims.content: At Level 3 (Social Value), the ego becomes more active and produces a characteristic persona protected by defense mechanisms.

claims.title: Level 4: ego reinforced by temptation
claims.content: At Level 4 (Imbalance), succumbing to a significant Characteristic Temptation reinforces the ego, increases defenses, and introduces imbalances.

claims.title: Regaining Level 1 qualities from Level 2 or 3
claims.content: While personality, ego, and defenses operate, a person can regain Level 1 qualities by overcoming the Basic Fear and relaxing ego activity.

claims.title: Level 1: liberation from Basic Fear
claims.content: At Level 1 (Liberation), a person who overcomes the Basic Fear moves beyond the ego and begins to actualize the true self.

claims.title: Seven levels of personality development
claims.content: Seven levels describe how a person moves from healthy liberation at Level 1 to violation at Level 7.

claims.title: Level 6: overcompensation and self-centeredness
claims.content: At Level 6 (Overcompensation), a person overcompensates for conflicts, showing self-centered, extreme behavior that others often find objectionable.

claims.title: Level 2: Basic Desire compensates for fear
claims.content: At Level 2 (Psychological Capacity), a person who succumbs to the Basic Fear develops a Basic Desire to compensate.

claims.title: Level 7: defenses break down
claims.content: At Level 7 (Violation), a major life crisis or abusive upbringing causes defenses to break down and compulsive survival tactics that violate the integrity of the self or others.

claims.title: Basic Desire: universal human need
claims.content: Basic Desire is a universal psychological human need that can also be understood as the ego ideal, and it is resolved only through contact with one's true nature.

claims.title: Level 2 traits by type
claims.content: Level 2 (Psychological Capacity and Sense of Self) core traits by type are: One Conscientiousness; Two Empathy; Three Adaptability; Four Self-Awareness; Five Observation; Six Engagement; Seven Responsiveness; Eight Self-Assertiveness; Nine Receptivity.

claims.title: Freedom decreases toward Level 9
claims.content: Personal freedom decreases as a person moves from Level 1 toward Level 9, and pathology is fundamentally unfree while health shows increasing personal freedom.

claims.title: Level 8 delusion and compulsion
claims.content: At Level 8, a person begins to lose touch with reality, becoming delusional in some way, and the resulting behavior is highly compulsive.

claims.title: Level 8 severe distortion and pathology
claims.content: At Level 8, anxiety causes severe intrapsychic conflict, and the person's thinking, perceiving, feeling and behavior become distorted and unfree, a fully pathological state.

claims.title: Comparing types within a level
claims.content: Core characteristics of each Level can be compared horizontally across the Enneagram types at the same Level of Development.

claims.title: Level 1 traits by type
claims.content: Level 1 (Liberation, Self-Transcendence) traits by type are: One Acceptance and Wisdom; Two Self-Nurturance and Unconditional love; Three Self-Acceptance and Authenticity; Four Self-Renewal and Inspiration; Five Clarity and Gnosis; Six Inner Guidance and Courage; Seven Assimilation and Gratitude; Eight Self-Surrender and Magnanimity; Nine Self-Remembering and Indomitable.

claims.title: Level 9 pathological destructiveness
claims.content: Level 9 is the level of pathological destructiveness, including psychosis, in which a person may destroy others, the self, or both to escape massive pain and anxiety.

claims.title: Level 4 imbalance traits by type
claims.content: Level 4 (Imbalance) core traits by type are: One constantly feeling personal obligation; Two people-pleasing; Three driving oneself to excel; Four living in imagination and heightened feelings; Five retreating into the mind; Six investing in external sources of security; Seven restlessness; Eight constantly asserting and pushing oneself; Nine avoiding conflict through accommodation.

claims.title: Level 3 traits by type
claims.content: Level 3 (Social Value, Contribution to Others) core traits by type are: One Principles and Responsibility; Two Generosity and Service; Three Ambition and Self-Development; Four Self-Revelation and Creativity; Five Focus and Innovation; Six Commitment and Cooperation; Seven Realism and Productivity; Eight Self-Confidence and Leadership; Nine Stability and Support.

claims.title: Level 1 direct felt experience
claims.content: At Level 1, a person experiences truth as felt reality rather than belief, and sees everything as it is without alteration or judgment.

claims.title: Personality octave and Essence octave
claims.content: Levels 2 through 9 form the octave of personality, and Level 1 is the first note of the higher octave of Essential Being.

claims.title: Level 1 as doorway to Essence
claims.content: Level 1, the Level of Liberation, is the doorway to Essential states, where a person rediscovers their connection with the Divine.

claims.title: Ego growth from Level 2
claims.content: The ego emerges at Level 2 and becomes increasingly inflated and destructive by Level 9.

claims.title: Personality Types: incremental method
claims.content: Personality Types presented the Enneagram types through an incremental method instead of a questionnaire.

claims.title: Enneagram level 6: overcompensation
claims.content: Level 6 of the Enneagram, characterized by overcompensation and defensive behavior, pairs each type with a trait and behavior: Type One Judgmentalism: Criticizing others; Type Two Self-importance: Patronization; Type Three Grandiosity: Self-Promotion; Type Four Exemption: Contempt; Type Five Extremism: Provocation; Type Six Authoritarianism: Assigning blame; Type Seven Self-Centeredness: Excessiveness; Type Eight Confrontational: Intimidation; Type Nine Resignation: Appeasement.

claims.title: Enneagram imbalance levels 5 to 9
claims.content: The Enneagram's imbalance levels 5 to 9 move from interpersonal control to pathological destructiveness.

claims.title: Self-administered questionnaires need sophistication
claims.content: Questionnaires to be administered by readers themselves should be more sophisticated than those usually found in self-help books.

claims.title: Enneagram level 8: delusions and compulsions
claims.content: Level 8 of the Enneagram, characterized by delusions and compulsions in thinking and behavior, pairs each type with a trait and behavior: Type One Obsession: Compulsive behavior; Type Two Entitlement: Coerciveness; Type Three Duplicity: Exploitation; Type Four Self-Hatred: Clinical depression; Type Five Schizoid withdrawal: Retreating behavior; Type Six Paranoia: Volatile behavior; Type Seven Manic mood swings: Reckless behavior; Type Eight Megalomania: Terrorizing behavior; Type Nine Dissociation: Disorientation.

claims.title: Chapter 5 questionnaire: update
claims.content: The questionnaire in Chapter 5 of Understanding the Enneagram is an update of the authors' first test instrument, with some statements revised and its basic structure kept.

claims.title: Enneagram level 7: violation
claims.content: Level 7 of the Enneagram, characterized by violation of self and others, pairs each type with a trait and behavior: Type One Self-Accusation: Intolerance of others; Type Two Self-Deception: Manipulation of others; Type Three Self-Rejection: Deception of others; Type Four Self-Sabotage: Hatred of others; Type Five Self-Negation: Rejection from others; Type Six Self-Betrayal: Defiance of others; Type Seven Self-Dissipation: Callousness with others; Type Eight Self-Hardening: Ruthlessness with others; Type Nine Self-Repression: Neglect of others.

claims.title: RHETI: Riso-Hudson Type Indicator
claims.content: RHETI stands for Riso-Hudson Type Indicator, a questionnaire available in the book Discovering Your Personality Type.

claims.title: Enneagram level 5: interpersonal control
claims.content: Level 5 of the Enneagram of imbalance, characterized by interpersonal control, pairs each type with a trait and behavior: Type One Self-Control: Rigid orderliness; Type Two Possessiveness: Intrusiveness; Type Three Image-Consciousness: Expediency; Type Four Self-Absorption: Temperamental; Type Five Preoccupation: Detachment; Type Six Ambivalence: Defensiveness; Type Seven Distraction: Hyperactivity; Type Eight Self-Glorification: Domination; Type Nine Disengagement: Complacency.

claims.title: Questionnaires: limited but useful evidence
claims.content: A questionnaire can never be foolproof, but it can provide valuable evidence for determining a person's Enneagram type or narrowing the choices.

claims.title: Accurate questionnaires need many items
claims.content: An accurate type questionnaire might need several hundred items and sophisticated statistical techniques to analyze the responses.

claims.title: Incremental method: needs self-knowledge
claims.content: The incremental method in Personality Types required some prior self-knowledge, so people with little self-awareness could not use it effectively.

claims.title: Questionnaires: time, errors, ambiguity
claims.content: Taking and grading a type questionnaire is time-consuming and can introduce errors, and even results from trained psychologists can be ambiguous or misleading.

claims.title: Enneagram level 9: pathological destructiveness
claims.content: Level 9 of the Enneagram, characterized by pathological destructiveness, pairs each type with a trait and behavior: Type One Condemnation: Retributive behavior; Type Two Conversion reactions: Psychosomatic problems; Type Three Psychopathy: Monomaniacal behavior; Type Four Clinical depression: Suicidal behavior; Type Five Psychotic states: Annihilating behavior; Type Six Self-Abasement: Self-destructive behavior; Type Seven Hysteria: Panicked behavior; Type Eight Sociopathy: Antisocial behavior; Type Nine Self-Abandonment: Depersonalized behavior.

claims.title: Incremental method: reader judgment
claims.content: The incremental method in Personality Types required readers to choose the description that fit them best and to judge whether it still fit as descriptions expanded.

claims.title: Discuss type with someone close
claims.content: Discussing a type frankly with someone who knows the person well can help even people confident of their type.

claims.title: Ask friends for type
claims.content: Friends can be asked which Enneagram type they think a person is.

claims.title: Rule: new patterns in relationships
claims.content: A chosen type that reveals new connections and patterns in one's self and relationships is probably accurate.

claims.title: Rule: family agreement
claims.content: If friends and family agree with a chosen type, the person is almost certainly on the right path.

claims.title: Healthy Twos show all traits
claims.content: Healthy Twos possess all the healthy traits listed in the Type Two Profile, acting on them consistently and at nearly the same time.

claims.title: Self-knowledge needed before progress
claims.content: Some self-knowledge is a prerequisite for making progress with the Enneagram.

claims.title: Rule: upset yet encouraged
claims.content: A chosen type that upsets but also encourages and excites a person is probably the correct choice.

claims.title: Rule: deep feelings and new insight
claims.content: A chosen type that stirs deep feelings and reveals previously unseen aspects of oneself is probably the correct type.

claims.title: Type cannot be certain
claims.content: No one can know with total assurance that a chosen Enneagram type is their true type.

claims.title: Choosing the type one wants
claims.content: People often choose the type they would like to be rather than the type they actually are.

claims.title: Type identified at different speeds
claims.content: Some people can determine their Enneagram type immediately, while others take longer.

claims.title: Narrow to two or three types
claims.content: People unsure of their Enneagram type should reflect on the two or three types they most likely fit.

claims.title: Confidence grows with experience
claims.content: Confidence in a person's self-assessment of type increases with time and experience.

claims.title: Emotional turmoil from self-understanding
claims.content: Understanding one's type and seeing oneself more objectively often causes emotional turmoil at first.

claims.title: Profiles as second questionnaire
claims.content: The Type Profiles can be read as a questionnaire by turning each word or phrase into a question.

claims.title: Others often see us better
claims.content: Others can often see a person more clearly than that person can see themselves.

claims.title: Profiles as checklists
claims.content: Each Type Profile is a checklist of statements that should be potentially true of a person all the time.

claims.title: Most identify type quickly
claims.content: Most people probably identify their Enneagram type correctly right away, though this is not established by controlled research.

claims.title: Questionnaire does not measure health
claims.content: Most questionnaire statements come from the upper-average, normal range and do not indicate a person's mental or emotional health, only basic personality type.

claims.title: Answer questionnaire spontaneously
claims.content: Questionnaire answers should be given spontaneously, without considering extreme circumstances under which a statement might be true.

claims.title: Identify type by whole pattern
claims.content: A personality type should be identified by discerning the whole pattern and the underlying motivations of each type.

claims.title: Isolated traits cause mistyping
claims.content: Choosing a personality type from a few isolated traits taken out of context often leads to mistyping.

claims.title: Integration and disintegration scores
claims.content: Scores on types in a person's Directions of Integration or Disintegration can be high alongside the wing and basic type scores.

claims.title: Basic type definition
claims.content: The basic type is the type that stands out most clearly in questionnaire scores.

claims.title: Full profile shows wing
claims.content: Scoring agreement for all nine types on the scoring sheet gives a full profile that indicates a person's wing.

claims.title: Nines score high on all types
claims.content: Many average Nines tend to score high on all types because their sense of self is characteristically undefined.

claims.title: Caricatures show type traits
claims.content: The caricatures in the book Personality Types and in the new book give visual impressions of each type and embody many of its traits.

claims.title: Wing definition
claims.content: A wing is the type on either side of a person's basic type that the person scored higher on in the questionnaire.

claims.title: Questionnaire organized by type
claims.content: The questionnaire is organized by type, and each personality type has twenty statements that reflect a range of healthy and average attitudes and behaviors.

claims.title: Extreme scores may signal misunderstanding
claims.content: Agreement with nearly all or none of the questionnaire statements may reflect misunderstanding the questions or an inability or unwillingness to discriminate between them.

claims.title: Thinking differs across types
claims.content: Thinking is a trait shared by every type, so it must be compared type by type, such as Fives and Nines.

claims.title: Fifteen agreements to determine type
claims.content: To determine a type with the questionnaire, a person should agree or strongly agree with fifteen or more of the twenty statements for that type.

claims.title: Type Two core statements
claims.content: Personality Type Two statements describe a person who loves others unconditionally and cares about their welfare.

claims.title: Type Three self-image: poised and outstanding
claims.content: Personality Type Three describes its self-image as self-assured, poised, and driven to be outstanding.

claims.title: Type Four: withdraws when vulnerable
claims.content: Personality Type Four describes withdrawing into a protective shell when feeling vulnerable or emotionally hurt.

claims.title: Type Three: fear of failure
claims.content: Personality Type Three describes a fear of failure hidden behind a confident appearance.

claims.title: Type Four self-image: authentic and aware
claims.content: Personality Type Four describes its self-image as sensitive, authentic, creative, and emotionally aware.

claims.title: Type Seven indulgence trait
claims.content: Personality Type Seven's self-descriptions state the person loves the good things in life and does not see why they should deny themselves.

claims.title: Type Six prudence and impulsiveness
claims.content: Personality Type Six's self-descriptions state the person can be extremely prudent about a problem yet sometimes act impulsively to finish it.

claims.title: Type Five love of knowledge
claims.content: Personality Type Five's self-descriptions state the person finds the life of the mind exciting and treasures the pursuit of knowledge.

claims.title: Type Seven variety-seeking trait
claims.content: Personality Type Seven's self-descriptions state the person keeps themselves amused by having many different things to do.

claims.title: Type Seven self-described traits
claims.content: Personality Type Seven's self-descriptions cover happiness, enthusiasm, many talents, practicality, and enjoying life's pleasures.

claims.title: Type Five perceives what others miss
claims.content: Personality Type Five's self-descriptions state the person perceives things that others miss or ignore.

claims.title: Type Six self-described traits
claims.content: Personality Type Six's self-descriptions cover loyalty, vigilance, reliability, self-doubt, trust issues, and prudence mixed with impulsiveness.

claims.title: Type Five foresight trait
claims.content: Personality Type Five's self-descriptions state the person can predict how things will turn out before they happen.

claims.title: Type Six difficulty trusting
claims.content: Personality Type Six's self-descriptions state the person spends much time trying to understand who and what they can trust.

claims.title: Type Five self-described traits
claims.content: Personality Type Five's self-descriptions cover insight, foresight, deep concentration, original ideas, and a preference for living alone.

claims.title: Type Five preference for solitude
claims.content: Personality Type Five's self-descriptions state it is safer and easier for the person to live alone and keep others from knowing their thoughts.

claims.title: Type Five deep concentration trait
claims.content: Personality Type Five's self-descriptions state the person can concentrate very deeply on work.

claims.title: Type Seven enthusiasm trait
claims.content: Personality Type Seven's self-descriptions state the person is enthusiastic about everything because everything seems to give pleasure.

claims.title: Type Six loyalty trait
claims.content: Personality Type Six's self-descriptions state the person is very committed to those who are committed to them.

claims.title: Type Six vigilance trait
claims.content: Personality Type Six's self-descriptions state the person is more vigilant about potential problems than most people.

claims.title: Type Eight direct manner
claims.content: Enneagram Type Eight describes itself as a passionate, direct person whose position is always clear to others.

claims.title: Type Eight seen as leader
claims.content: Enneagram Type Eight describes itself as strong and decisive, so others look to it for leadership.

claims.title: Type One good judgment
claims.content: Enneagram Type One describes itself as having very good judgment and being extremely prudent.

claims.title: Type Eight rallies others
claims.content: Enneagram Type Eight describes itself as able to see opportunities and rally others to achieve how it wants things to be.

claims.title: Type Nine assertive and close
claims.content: Enneagram Type Nine describes itself as able to assert itself at its best while staying close to people, especially its spouse and children.

claims.title: Type Eight self-confidence
claims.content: Enneagram Type Eight describes itself as self-assertive with a lot of self-confidence.

claims.title: Type Nine warm atmosphere
claims.content: Enneagram Type Nine describes itself as enjoying a warm, supportive atmosphere in which others can flourish.

claims.title: Type One strong conscience
claims.content: Enneagram Type One describes itself as having a strong conscience and a clear sense of right and wrong.

claims.title: Type Eight enjoys danger
claims.content: Enneagram Type Eight describes itself as liking the thrill of danger and adventure and often succeeding despite the odds.

claims.title: Type Eight self-descriptions overview
claims.content: Enneagram Type Eight self-descriptions cover self-assertiveness, leadership, decisiveness, love of challenge, and a direct manner.

claims.title: Type Nine self-descriptions overview
claims.content: Enneagram Type Nine self-descriptions cover asserting oneself while staying close to others, creating a warm atmosphere, and contentment.

claims.title: Type One self-descriptions overview
claims.content: Enneagram Type One self-descriptions cover good judgment, prudence, and a strong conscience.

claims.title: Type Nine optimism and contentment
claims.content: Enneagram Type Nine describes itself as optimistic and contented with itself and its life as it is.

claims.title: Wing and variant shape type expression
claims.content: The wing and the Instinctual Variant can significantly affect a person's behavior and how they express their Enneagram type.

claims.title: Type identification is a learnable skill
claims.content: Accurately determining Enneagram personality types is an art that anyone can become proficient in with time and practice.

claims.title: Enneagram interpretations contain contradictions
claims.content: Current Enneagram interpretations in circulation contain significant contradictions and misattributions of traits from type to type.

claims.title: Many variations make types similar
claims.content: The Enneagram can accommodate more than 486 variations of its types, so some of those variations are inevitably similar.

claims.title: Complexity causes Enneagram misidentification
claims.content: Misidentifying Enneagram types is easy because the Enneagram is complex and human nature is even more complex.

claims.title: Sixes and Eights resemble each other
claims.content: Enneagram Type Six at Level 6 (Authoritarian Rebel) can resemble Type Eight at Level 6 (Confrontational Adversary), because both are belligerent and authoritarian in noticeably different ways.

claims.title: Nines are not always peaceful
claims.content: Healthy Enneagram Type Nine is often peaceful and serene, but Nines can also be angry, aggressive, and anxious.

claims.title: How Nines express anger
claims.content: When Enneagram Type Nines are angry, they often express it as coolness toward the person and deny being angry, and severe outbursts can erupt suddenly and subside quickly.

claims.title: Misidentification limits Enneagram benefit
claims.content: If a person misidentifies their Enneagram type, the Enneagram will do them little good for self-understanding.

claims.title: Incomplete information hinders type inference
claims.content: Inferring a person's Enneagram type from less than complete information makes identification difficult.

claims.title: Long-term observation identifies type
claims.content: A person's type is best identified from traits shown in long-term behavior, observed over time and in a variety of circumstances.

claims.title: Types are complex and take time
claims.content: Enneagram types are not static or simple, and understanding all their subtleties and variations takes time and dedication.

claims.title: Compare trait observations with others
claims.content: Discussing observed traits with others helps check whether perceptions agree when identifying a person's type.

claims.title: Personal knowledge helps but is optional
claims.content: Knowing an individual personally helps identify that person's type but is not absolutely necessary.

claims.title: Center of gravity varies by few Levels
claims.content: A person's center of gravity on the Levels of Development varies by no more than a few Levels.

claims.title: High-functioning people are harder to identify
claims.content: High-functioning people are harder to identify because they are less identified with their type's patterns and can express a wider range of coping styles.

claims.title: Same-type people look alike
claims.content: People of the same type, particularly those with the same wing, are noticeably similar to each other.

claims.title: Motives distinguish similar behavior
claims.content: Different types can act in virtually identical ways while having different motives, so underlying motives matter more than superficial behavior.

claims.title: Famous-person diagnoses are educated guesses
claims.content: The type diagnoses of famous people in Personality Types are educated guesses based on reading, intuition, and observation, not infallible judgments.

claims.title: Two skills for typing people
claims.content: Identifying a person's type requires learning which traits go with which types and how to recognize those traits in individuals.

claims.title: Reagan assessed as Type Nine
claims.content: Ronald Reagan is assessed as a Type Nine, based on consistently observed genial, unassuming, optimistic, and easygoing behavior.

claims.title: Levels of Development defined
claims.content: Levels of Development are graded stages along which a person's behavior moves, from healthy traits toward the extremes of unhealth.

claims.title: No one shows every trait at once
claims.content: No one manifests all the traits of his or her type at one time, and very few people traverse the entire Continuum.

claims.title: Stress can shift toward disintegration type
claims.content: Under prolonged stress, a person may strongly behave like, and feel like, the type in his or her Direction of Disintegration.

claims.title: Ones and Threes: shared traits
claims.content: Average Ones and average Threes are sometimes mistaken because both are efficient, highly organized, and task-oriented.

claims.title: Ones and Threes: motivation contrast
claims.content: Average Ones are idealists who strive for perfection and order, while average Threes are efficient pragmatists who focus more on goals than on standards.

claims.title: Gender and One-Two mistyping
claims.content: Women who are 1w2s tend to see themselves as 2w1s, and men who are 2w1s may see themselves as 1w2s.

claims.title: Ones and Threes: concealing feelings
claims.content: Average Threes are more able to mask their feelings and rarely appear emotionally disturbed for long, while Ones are far less able to conceal irritation and disappointment.

claims.title: Ones and Threes: adaptability
claims.content: Ones tend to be attached to particular methods, while Threes are more adaptable and change tactics quickly when they do not get the desired result.

claims.title: Ones and Twos: style contrast
claims.content: Ones try to transcend the personal and appeal to principles, while Twos see their service in personal terms and seek close connection and merging.

claims.title: Ones and Threes: core drives
claims.content: Ones try to be perfect to fend off their own superegos, while Threes try to excel to overcome feelings of family shame.

claims.title: Ones and Twos: wing confusion
claims.content: Ones and Twos are sometimes confused when a wing is mistaken for the dominant type, with 1w2s occasionally mistyped as 2w1s.

claims.title: Average Threes: detachment from feelings
claims.content: Average Threes show detachment from their feelings rather than suppression, and they present whatever emotion seems appropriate to the situation.

claims.title: One and Three negative emotions
claims.content: Ones' most prevalent negative emotions are righteous anger, indignation, irritation, and guilt, while Threes' are hostility, arrogance, and underlying shame and humiliation.

claims.title: Average Ones: sublimated feelings
claims.content: Average Ones appear to hold deeper feelings in check and may sublimate them into activities such as organizing or volunteering.

claims.title: Ones and Twos: emotional expression
claims.content: Ones defend their autonomy and are restrained in expressing positive feelings, while Twos have difficulty with hostile feelings and are fairly unrestrained in expressing positive feelings.

claims.title: Threes: projected charm
claims.content: Threes are more skilled than Ones at projecting charm, and their underlying detachment shows in how abruptly they shift affect between situations and people.

claims.title: Ones and Threes goal approach
claims.content: Enneagram Type One tries to find the objective means that will best lead to its ideal, while Enneagram Type Three works backward from its goal to the most efficient means.

claims.title: Ones mistaken for Fours
claims.content: A One who is moving toward Enneagram Type Four under stress may come to believe that they are a Four.

claims.title: Misidentification focuses on unhealthy traits
claims.content: Ones who mistake themselves for Fours focus almost exclusively on the traits of unhealthy Fours rather than on the type as a whole.

claims.title: Average Ones criticism and irritation
claims.content: Average Enneagram Type One people are frequently critical and irritable, usually over others' inefficiency or failure to follow agreed-upon procedures.

claims.title: Ones and Fours shared traits
claims.content: Enneagram Type One and Enneagram Type Four both tend to be perfectionistic and dissatisfied with things as they are.

claims.title: Ones vulnerable to depression
claims.content: Enneagram Type One is one of the types more vulnerable to depression.

claims.title: Fours feelings before duties
claims.content: Enneagram Type Four wants to work through its feelings before meeting its duties, which may make it difficult to mobilize itself to meet responsibilities.

claims.title: Ones focus on practical results
claims.content: Enneagram Type One people are primarily people of action and are interested only in ideas that lead to a practical result.

claims.title: Fives value ideas over practice
claims.content: Enneagram Type Five is primarily a mental type that can ponder any proposition and does not particularly care about its practical ramifications.

claims.title: Ones under difficulty
claims.content: When Enneagram Type One people experience difficulties, they are typically guilt-ridden, feel worthless, and experience intense self-contempt and self-hatred.

claims.title: Type One moral perfection
claims.content: Enneagram Type One offers itself as an example of striving for moral perfection and sees its members as people who can meet the highest standards.

claims.title: Fours punish by withdrawing
claims.content: When upset, Enneagram Type Four attempts to punish offenders by coldly withdrawing emotionally or physically and refusing further communication.

claims.title: Ones and Fives Jungian correspondence
claims.content: Enneagram Type One corresponds to Jung's extroverted thinking type, and Enneagram Type Five corresponds to the introverted, or subjective, thinking type.

claims.title: Type Three individual perfection
claims.content: Enneagram Type Three offers itself as an example of individual perfection, particularly personal desirability, and as a person who can accomplish and be the best.

claims.title: Ones: thinking defends beliefs
claims.content: Average to unhealthy Ones think in order to buttress beliefs they have already established.

claims.title: Inner Critic and Inner Committee
claims.content: The source says Ones have an Inner Critic in their heads, while Sixes have an Inner Committee.

claims.title: Ones: convinced and respect conviction
claims.content: Average to unhealthy Ones are entirely convinced of the rightness of their views and respect people who hold similar conviction.

claims.title: Ones: certain and persuasive
claims.content: Average Ones are certain of their views and try to convince others that they know the optimal way to do things.

claims.title: Fives: uncertainty and reversed theories
claims.content: Average to unhealthy Fives get lost in uncertainty, developing elaborate theories and overturning them soon after.

claims.title: Fives: detached from practical world
claims.content: Average Fives become detached from the practical world and involved with complex mental constructs.

claims.title: Unhealthy Fives: arguing to feel smart
claims.content: Unhealthy Fives may argue points they do not personally agree with to feel smarter than others.

claims.title: Ones and Sixes: shared guilt
claims.content: Both Ones and Sixes tend to feel guilty when they act against their ideals (Ones) or their commitments to allies, beliefs, and authorities (Sixes).

claims.title: Ones: decisive and opinionated
claims.content: Average Ones are not indecisive: they know their own minds and freely express opinions on everything.

claims.title: Ones and Sixes: compliance sources
claims.content: Ones and Sixes are both compliant types, but Ones comply with their superegos and ideals, while Sixes comply with their superegos and other people, especially allies or authority figures.

claims.title: Fives: losing assessment of ideas
claims.content: As average Fives become more absorbed in their own mental landscapes, they lose the capacity to accurately assess the truth or significance of their ideas.

claims.title: Sixes: anxious and reactive
claims.content: Average Sixes are anxious, indecisive, ambivalent, and above all reactive.

claims.title: Ones and Fives: certainty difference
claims.content: Ones and Fives differ most in the One's emphasis on certainty and judgment and the Five's relative lack of certainty and difficulty with discernment.

claims.title: Inner Committee definition
claims.content: Inner Committee is the source's term for the internal voice of multiple authorities that Sixes have in their heads.

claims.title: Opinions rooted in instincts
claims.content: The source states that opinions and beliefs have their basis in the instincts, in the gut.

claims.title: Ones and Fives: love of knowledge
claims.content: Ones and Fives both are philosophical and love knowledge: Ones to perfect the world, Fives to discover more about it.

claims.title: Ones: thinking toward ideals
claims.content: Ones use thinking to relate to their ideals, focusing on rules and procedures for improving themselves and their world.

claims.title: Ones: reserved but principled
claims.content: Average Ones are cool, impersonal, and overly reserved, yet keenly interested in applying their principles to daily life.

claims.title: Fives: provocative views to unsettle
claims.content: Less healthy Fives assert provocative views mainly to disturb others' certainty rather than to convince them.

claims.title: Ones and Sixes: emotional tone
claims.content: Ones and Sixes are easy to distinguish by the overall emotional tone of each type.

claims.title: Ones deductive, Fives inductive
claims.content: Ones are deductive, reasoning from principles to specific applications, while Fives are inductive, reasoning from given data to broader theories.

claims.title: Inner Critic definition
claims.content: Inner Critic is the source's term for the internal critical voice that Ones have in their heads.

claims.title: Ones judge ideals, Fives question
claims.content: Average Ones judge situations by idealistic standards based on what they think should be the case, while Fives question assumptions and standards.

claims.title: Ones teachers, Fives inventors
claims.content: Ones tend to be teachers and moralists, while Fives tend to be inventors and iconoclasts.

claims.title: Judgment central to Ones, not Fives
claims.content: Judgment is not as centrally important to Fives as it is to Ones.

claims.title: Ones: controlled, orderly tone
claims.content: Average Ones have a self-controlled, impersonal, efficient emotional tone that values orderliness and propriety.

claims.title: Ones keep feelings at bay
claims.content: Average Enneagram Type One individuals are often so tightly self-controlled that they keep their feelings at bay and are frequently unaware of the degree of their tensions.

claims.title: Sevens usually optimistic
claims.content: Enneagram Type Seven individuals are usually very optimistic about the future and about things working out positively.

claims.title: Sixes give orders from fear
claims.content: Enneagram Type Six individuals can give orders because they fear that others' erratic conduct may disrupt the security and stability they seek, not from rigid inner standards.

claims.title: Sixes internalize authority values
claims.content: Enneagram Type Six individuals identify with certain beliefs or authority figures and internalize the values they learn from those sources of guidance.

claims.title: Ones and Sixes confusion source
claims.content: Confusion about distinguishing Enneagram Types One and Six seems to stem from both types having overactive superegos.

claims.title: Ones order others to improve
claims.content: Enneagram Type One individuals do not hesitate to order others around, telling them what they should do to improve themselves or be more effective.

claims.title: Ones frustrated by plan changes
claims.content: Enneagram Type One individuals get frustrated when plans change and usually do not like to deviate from careful preparations.

claims.title: Sevens sometimes mistype as Ones
claims.content: Enneagram Type One individuals are unlikely to mistype themselves as Type Seven, but Type Seven individuals occasionally mistype themselves as Ones.

claims.title: Sevens driven by anxiety
